text: Medical Assistance Community members who need medical assistance are directed to medical assistance. > Identify and coordinate community resources that can be used to assist and treat the injured. > Identify and check on people with day-to-day medical needs. > Direct the community to medical providers that are known to be open. > Identify and coordinate people in the community with medical skills who can help. In all life-threatening situations, attempt to contact the emergency services by calling 111. Injured and sick people should go to the nearest open medical centre first. People with first aid skills should go to their nearest open medical centre or go to the Hub. Check on your neighbours and people who may need extra help.

text: causing organisms. If water is cloudy, filter it through a clean cloth. Boil water for one minute, let it cool, and store it in clean containers with covers. IF YOU CAN’T BOIL: ADD BLEACH. Bleach will kill some (not all) types of disease-causing organisms. Just like boiling, filter cloudy water though a clean cloth first. Use only regular, unscented, liquid household bleach. Add two drops of bleach per litre of water. Stir well, let stand for 30 minutes before using, then store in clean containers with covers.

section: Community Response Plan and Emergency Hub Guide
text: This Community Response Plan works alongside the Community Emergency Hub Guide. The Hub Guide provides guidance on how your community can organise and support one another during an emergency. Use the Hub Guide and your Community Response Plan together to organise your community response. You will ﬁnd the Hub Guide in the Hub kit along with Hub role lanyards, stationery, a map, an AM/FM radio, and a VHF radio.

text: Your community has all the skills, resources, local knowledge and relationships to support one another during an emergency. text: Medical Assistance Community members who need medical assistance are directed to medical assistance. > Identify and coordinate community resources that can be used to assist and treat the injured. > Identify and check on people with day-to-day medical needs. > Direct the community to medical providers that are known to be open. > Identify and coordinate people in the community with medical skills who can help. In all life-threatening situations, attempt to contact the emergency services by calling 111. Injured and sick people should go to the nearest open medical centre ﬁrst. text: treat. BEST CHOICE: BOIL. Boiling water will kill most types of disease- causing organisms. If water is cloudy, ﬁlter it through a clean cloth. Boil water for one minute, let it cool, and store it in clean containers with covers. IF YOU CAN’T BOIL: ADD BLEACH. Bleach will kill some (not all) types of disease-causing organisms. Just like boiling, ﬁlter cloudy water though a clean cloth ﬁrst. Use only regular, unscented, liquid household bleach. Add two drops of bleach per litre of water. Stir well, let stand for 30 minutes before using, then store in clean containers with covers.

Water reserviours are all around the region but automatically seal if lines are damaged. Technicians must manually attend to the valves. This will take time so look for other sources of water within the community right away. Some schools and community centres have large water tanks installed. If there is one in your community check to see what their plan is for using the water. Local streams and open bodies of water are not reliable sources of clean water. section: people can’t stay at homes or with friends?
text: Treat any non-bottled water. Boil it if you can, if not use bleach to treat. BEST CHOICE: BOIL. Boiling water will kill most types of disease- causing organisms. If water is cloudy, filter it through a clean cloth. Boil water for one minute, let it cool, and store it in clean containers with covers. IF YOU CAN’T BOIL: ADD BLEACH. Bleach will kill some (not all) types of disease-causing organisms. Just like boiling, filter cloudy water though a clean cloth first. Use only regular, unscented, liquid household bleach. Add two drops of bleach per litre of water. Stir well, let stand for 30 minutes before using, then store in clean containers with covers.
source_ref: Clifton Terrace - Clifton Terrace Sch Community Response Plan (reviewed 2026-07)

text: Local streams and open bodies of water are not reliable sources of clean water. Chemical pollution and heavy metal contamination is not removed by boiling water or adding bleach. Treat any non-bottled water. Boil it if you can, if not use bleach to treat. BEST CHOICE: BOIL. Boiling water will kill most types of disease- causing organisms. If water is cloudy, filter it through a clean cloth. Boil water for one minute, let it cool, and store it in clean containers with covers. IF YOU CAN’T BOIL: ADD BLEACH. Bleach will kill some (not all) types of disease-causing organisms. Just like boiling, filter cloudy water though a clean cloth first. Use only regular, unscented, liquid household bleach. text: Treat any non-bottled water. Boil it if you can, if not use bleach to treat. BEST CHOICE: BOIL. Boiling water will kill most types of disease- causing organisms. If water is cloudy, filter it through a clean cloth. Boil water for one minute, let it cool, and store it in clean containers with covers. IF YOU CAN’T BOIL: ADD BLEACH. Bleach will kill some (not all) types of disease-causing organisms. Just like boiling, filter cloudy water though a clean cloth first. Use only regular, unscented, liquid household bleach. Add two drops of bleach per litre of water. Stir well, let stand for 30 minutes before using, then store in clean containers with covers.

text: > Coordinate community water sources for drinking, cooking and hygiene. > Arrange a place in the community where water can be distributed if needed. Water reserviours are all around the region but automatically seal if lines are damaged. Technicians must manually attend to the valves. This will take time so look for other sources of water within the community right away. Some schools and community centres have large water tanks installed. If there is one in your community check to see what their plan is for using the water. Local streams and open bodies of water are not reliable sources of clean water. Chemical pollution and heavy metal contamination is not removed by boiling water or adding bleach.
source_ref: Karori - Karori Community Centre Community Response Plan (reviewed 2026-07)

section: people can’t stay at homes or with friends?
text: Treat any non-bottled water. Boil it if you can, if not use bleach to treat. BEST CHOICE: BOIL. Boiling water will kill most types of disease- causing organisms. If water is cloudy, filter it through a clean cloth. Boil water for one minute, let it cool, and store it in clean containers with covers. IF YOU CAN’T BOIL: ADD BLEACH. Bleach will kill some (not all) types of disease-causing organisms. Just like boiling, filter cloudy water though a clean cloth first. Use only regular, unscented, liquid household bleach. Add two drops of bleach per litre of water. Stir well, let stand for 30 minutes before using, then store in clean containers with covers.
source_ref: Karori - Karori Community Centre Community Response Plan (reviewed 2026-07)

section: people can’t stay at homes or with friends?
text: Treat any non-bottled water. Boil it if you can, if not use bleach to treat. BEST CHOICE: BOIL. Boiling water will kill most types of disease- causing organisms. If water is cloudy, filter it through a clean cloth. Boil water for one minute, let it cool, and store it in clean containers with covers. IF YOU CAN’T BOIL: ADD BLEACH. Bleach will kill some (not all) types of disease-causing organisms. Just like boiling, filter cloudy water though a clean cloth first. Use only regular, unscented, liquid household bleach. Add two drops of bleach per litre of water. Stir well, let stand for 30 minutes before using, then store in clean containers with covers.

text: Water reserviours are all around the region but automatically seal if lines are damaged. Technicians must manually attend to the valves. This will take time so look for other sources of water within the community right away. Some schools and community centres have large water tanks installed. If there is one in your community check to see what their plan is for using the water. Local streams and open bodies of water are not reliable sources of clean water. Chemical pollution and heavy metal contamination is not removed by boiling water or adding bleach. Treat any non-bottled water. Boil it if you can, if not use bleach to treat. BEST CHOICE: BOIL. Boiling water will kill most types of disease-
source_ref: Khandallah - Cashmere Avenue School Community Response Plan (reviewed 2025-04)

section: people can’t stay at homes or with friends?
text: causing organisms. If water is cloudy, ﬁlter it through a clean cloth. Boil water for one minute, let it cool, and store it in clean containers with covers. IF YOU CAN’T BOIL: ADD BLEACH. Bleach will kill some (not all) types of disease-causing organisms. Just like boiling, ﬁlter cloudy water though a clean cloth ﬁrst. Use only regular, unscented, liquid household bleach. Add two drops of bleach per litre of water. Stir well, let stand for 30 minutes before using, then store in clean containers with covers.

text: Local streams and open bodies of water are not reliable sources of clean water. Chemical pollution and heavy metal contamination is not removed by boiling water or adding bleach. Treat any non-bottled water. Boil it if you can, if not use bleach to treat. BEST CHOICE: BOIL. Boiling water will kill most types of disease- causing organisms. If water is cloudy, filter it through a clean cloth. Boil water for one minute, let it cool, and store it in clean containers with covers. IF YOU CAN’T BOIL: ADD BLEACH. Bleach will kill some (not all) types of disease-causing organisms. Just like boiling, filter cloudy water though a clean cloth first. Use only regular, unscented, liquid household bleach. Water reserviours are all around the region but automatically seal if lines are damaged. Technicians must manually attend to the valves. This will take time so look for other sources of water within the community right away. Some schools and community centres have large water tanks installed. If there is one in your community check to see what their plan is for using the water. Local streams and open bodies of water are not reliable sources of clean water. Chemical pollution and heavy metal contamination is not removed by boiling water or adding bleach.
source_ref: Ngaio - Ngaio School Community Response Plan (reviewed 2026-07)

section: people can’t stay at homes or with friends?
text: Treat any non-bottled water. Boil it if you can, if not use bleach to treat. BEST CHOICE: BOIL. Boiling water will kill most types of disease- causing organisms. If water is cloudy, filter it through a clean cloth. Boil water for one minute, let it cool, and store it in clean containers with covers. IF YOU CAN’T BOIL: ADD BLEACH. Bleach will kill some (not all) types of disease-causing organisms. Just like boiling, filter cloudy water though a clean cloth first. Use only regular, unscented, liquid household bleach. Add two drops of bleach per litre of water. Stir well, let stand for 30 minutes before using, then store in clean containers with covers.
source_ref: Ngaio - Ngaio School Community Response Plan (reviewed 2026-07)

text: Local streams and open bodies of water are not reliable sources of clean water. Chemical pollution and heavy metal contamination is not removed by boiling water or adding bleach. Treat any non-bottled water. Boil it if you can, if not use bleach to treat. BEST CHOICE: BOIL. Boiling water will kill most types of disease-causing organisms. If water is cloudy, ﬁlter it through a clean cloth. Boil water for one minute, let it cool, and store it in clean containers with covers. IF YOU CAN’T BOIL: ADD BLEACH. Bleach will kill some (not all) types of disease-causing organisms. Just like boiling, ﬁlter cloudy water though a clean cloth ﬁrst. Use only regular, unscented, liquid household bleach. Add two drops of bleach per litre of water. Stir well, let stand for 30 minutes before using, then store in clean containers with covers.

Water reserviours are all around the region but automatically seal if lines are damaged. Technicians must manually attend to the valves. This will take time so look for other sources of water within the community right away. Some schools and community centres have large water tanks installed. If there is one in your community check to see what their plan is for using the water. Local streams and open bodies of water are not reliable sources of clean water. Chemical pollution and heavy metal contamination is not removed by boiling water or adding bleach.

text: Treat any non-bottled water. Boil it if you can, if not use bleach to treat. BEST CHOICE: BOIL. Boiling water will kill most types of disease- causing organisms. If water is cloudy, filter it through a clean cloth. Boil water for one minute, let it cool, and store it in clean containers with covers. IF YOU CAN’T BOIL: ADD BLEACH. Bleach will kill some (not all) types of disease-causing organisms. Just like boiling, filter cloudy water though a clean cloth first. Use only regular, unscented, liquid household bleach. Add two drops of bleach per litre of water. Stir well, let stand for 30 minutes before using, then store in clean containers with covers.
source_ref: Paraparaumu West - St Pauls Church Community Response Plan (reviewed 2025-10)

text: Treat any non-bottled water. Boil it if you can, if not use bleach to treat. BEST CHOICE: BOIL. Boiling water will kill most types of disease- causing organisms. If water is cloudy, filter it through a clean cloth. Boil water for one minute, let it cool, and store it in clean containers with covers. IF YOU CAN’T BOIL: ADD BLEACH. Bleach will kill some (not all) types of disease-causing organisms. Just like boiling, filter cloudy water though a clean cloth first. Use only regular, unscented, liquid household bleach. Add two drops of bleach per litre of water. Stir well, let stand for 30 minutes before using, then store in clean containers with covers.

Local streams and open bodies of water are not reliable sources of clean water. Chemical pollution and heavy metal contamination is not removed by boiling water or adding bleach. Small repairs may make homes safe enough to stay in. If people need to leave their homes, encourage them to take as much bedding as possible. Encourage people to stay with friends and family if possible. Ask neighbours or others in their street if they have a spare room. People in the community may have spare beds, air mattresses, and couches available to offer people without a place to stay. Check gas and electricity supplies are safe to use. Turn gas off at
source_ref: Waikanae East - Waikanae Memorial Hall Community Response Plan (reviewed 2025-10)

Are there simple repairs that could be done to make a home safe enough for people to stay there. Youmay have visitors to your community who don’t live locally - commuters, shoppers, employees etc. These are the people most likely to need accommodation in your community. text: Local streams and open bodies of water are not reliable sources of clean water. Chemical pollution and heavy metal contamination is not removed by boiling water or adding bleach. Treat any non-bottled water. Boil it if you can, if not use bleach to treat. BEST CHOICE: BOIL. Boiling water will kill most types of disease- causing organisms. If water is cloudy, filter it through a clean cloth. Boil water for one minute, let it cool, and store it in clean containers with covers. IF YOU CAN’T BOIL: ADD BLEACH. Bleach will kill some (not all) types of disease-causing organisms. Just like boiling, filter cloudy water though a clean cloth first. Use only regular, unscented, liquid household bleach. section: Community Response Plan and Emergency Hub Guide
text: This Community Response Plan works alongside the Community Emergency Hub Guide. The Hub Guide provides guidance on how your community can organise and support one another during an emergency. Use the Hub Guide and your Community Response Plan together to organise your community response. You will find the Hub Guide in the Hub kit along with Hub role lanyards, stationery, a map, an AM/FM radio, and a VHF radio.
source_ref: Worser Bay - Worser Bay School Community Response Plan (reviewed 2025-11)

text: Your community has all the skills, resources, local knowledge and relationships to support one another during an emergency. You can utilise these by working together at your local Community Emergency Hub. Use this document as a starting point for solutions to community needs and your response as a community. text: contamination is not removed by boiling water or adding bleach. Treat any non-bottled water. Boil it if you can, if not use bleach to treat. BEST CHOICE: BOIL. Boiling water will kill most types of disease- causing organisms. If water is cloudy, filter it through a clean cloth. Boil water for one minute, let it cool, and store it in clean containers with covers. IF YOU CAN’T BOIL: ADD BLEACH. Bleach will kill some (not all) types of disease-causing organisms. Just like boiling, filter cloudy water though a clean cloth first. Use only regular, unscented, liquid household bleach. Add two drops of bleach per litre of water. Stir well, let stand for 30 minutes before using, then store in clean containers with covers.
